description.value: A cross-sectional structural MRI and voxel-based morphometry study characterising multidimensional apathy and its neural correlates across Alzheimer’s disease, behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls.

spans.text: Here, we employed a cross-sectional design to characterise the multidimensional nature of apathy across syndromes and disease course.

value: AD patients would show predominantly executive apathy, whereas bvFTD patients would show both executive and emotional apathy.
With disease progression, however, it was hypothesised that apathy profiles in AD and bvFTD would likely encompass all dimensions as atrophy extends throughout the brain.
We hypothesised that frontal subcortical structures would be associated with apathy severity.

Specifically, we predicted that emotional apathy would be associated with integrity of orbital and medial frontal regions, executive apathy with integrity of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and initiation apathy with integrity of the basal ganglia.
Finally, we hypothesised that apathy and depression would be separable clinical phenomena, although these symptoms might co-exist in some individual patients.
